Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ is a ___ year old female who is s/p 2 kidney

#. Acute humoral rejection - The patient was found to have an 
elevated creatinine at ___ clinic on ___.  She was 
admitted to ___ and a renal biopsy was performed to evaluate 
for the possibility of rejection.  The renal biopsy showed e/o 
acute humoral rejection and the patient was started on a course 
of plasmapheresis and steroids.  A tunneled catheter was placed 
for the pheresis.  DSAs were sent.  Over the course of her 
hospital course, the patient underwent multiple pheresis 
sessions.  Over the first 3 days of her stay, Ms. ___ also 
received 500mg solumedrol which was tapered over her stay to 
20mg of prednisone.  Her creatinine remained elevated (>2.5) and 
the decision was made to start ATG.  Ms. ___ received 4 
sessions of ATG treatment.  On discharge, the patient's 
creatinine remained elevated.  She is otherwise asymptomatic and 
will follow-up with her tranplant nephrologist. 

#. Hypertension - The patient has baseline HTN which is treated 
at home with amlodipine, lisinopril and labetolol.  Lisinopril 
was held in the setting of high Cr.  During the ___ 
hospital stay, she was noted to have high BPs (in the 160-170s 
systolic).  It was believed that the elevated BPs were secondary 
to steroids and fluid overload from pheresis.  She was started 
on a course of diuretics and her labetolol dosage was increased. 
 The patient's BPs improved and she felt subjectively less fluid 
overloaded with decreased SOB and edema.  The patient was 
discharged on 600mg labetolol 3x daily and 20mg furosemide.  
Lisinopril was not restarted.       

#. High ___ - The patient had elevated ___ while in house.  Likely 
___ steroid therapy.  She was started on glipizide 2.5mg BID 
while in house and will continue this as an outpatient.  Also 
will continue humalog with meals as an outpatient as needed.  

#. Kidney Transplant - As above, the patient is s/p 2 kidney 
transplants needed due to a ureteral congenital abnormality 
leading to renal failure.  She lost her first kidney to 
rejection.  In house, the patient's tacro levels were followed 
and she was continued on bactrim PPX.  The patient was 
discharged with prograf dosing of 6.5mg BID.  

#. Hyperlipidemia - No active issues.  Continued on home 
regimen.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with history of renal failure, status post
second transplant.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the left lower
quadrant transplant were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Renal transplant ultrasound from ___.

FINDINGS:
The left lower quadrant renal transplant measures 13.2 cm without evidence of
perinephric fluid collections or suspicious masses.  There is new, mild
hydronephrosis.  The resistive indices of the main, upper, mid and lower pole
renal arteries range from 0.76-0.80 and are slightly elevated.  The waveforms
show mild parvus tardus.  The main renal vein is patent.

Urinary bladder is mildly filled and appears normal.

IMPRESSION:
1.  New, mild hydronephrosis.
2.  Slightly elevated RIs.

FINDINGS WERE COMMUNICATED TO ___. ___ AT 4.30 ___ BY ___. ___.

PROCEDURE:  Ultrasound guidance for renal transplant biopsy performed by renal
team.

INDICATION:  Rule out rejection.  Patient is status post two renal
transplants.  Abnormal renal function.

TECHNIQUE:  
Ultrasound guidance was provided to the renal physicians performing the left
lower quadrant renal transplant non-targeted biopsy.  Under ultrasound
guidance an entrance site was selected and the lower pole of the left lower
quadrant renal transplant kidney was selected and targeted.  Two 18-gauge core
biopsies were obtained and were sent to pathology at the time of the
procedure.  Please refer to nephrologist note for details of the procedure.
There were no immediate complications.  The patient did not receive moderate
sedation during the procedure.

IMPRESSION:  Ultrasound guidance provided for renal MD performing left lower
quadrant renal transplant biopsy.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with renal transplant with reaction requiring
urgent plasmapheresis.

CLINICIANS:  Drs. ___ and ___ performed the procedure. 
___ was present and supervising throughout.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed throughout the total intraservice time
of 45 minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored.  Local anesthesia was provided by 1% lidocaine to the
dermis and 1% lidocaine with epinephrine into the subcutaneous tissues.

PROCEDURE:  Written informed consent was obtained from the patient after
explaining the risks, benefits, and indications of the procedure.  The patient
was transported to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging
table.  The right neck was prepped and draped in the standard sterile fashion.
A preprocedural huddle and timeout were performed per ___ protocol.

After anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues, a micropuncture needle
was inserted into the right internal jugular vein under ultrasound guidance. 
Hard copy ultrasound images were saved for reference.  A 0.018 nitinol wire
was advanced into the SVC.  After additional local anesthesia, a small ___
was made in the skin.  Micropuncture needle was exchanged for a micropuncture
sheath.  The inner cannula and nitinol wire were removed.  A 0.035 J wire was
advanced into the right atrium.  Appropriate measurements were made for a skin
incision four fingerbreadths below the venotomy site.  The wire was then
advanced into the IVC and right hepatic vein.

Attention was now turned to creation of a subcutaneous tunnel.  After
additional local anesthesia, a 1-cm skin incision was made.  A 19-cm
tip-to-cuff dual-lumen tunneled hemodialysis catheter was passed from the
incision to the venotomy site with the aid of a tunneling device.  The
venotomy tract was serially dilated with 10 and ___ dilators.  During
the process, the J wire was advanced into the IVC.  A peel-away sheath was
passed over the Amplatz wire.  The wire and inner cannula were removed and the
hemodialysis catheter was passed through the peel-away sheath.  The peel-away
sheath was removed while advancing the catheter into the right atrium.  This
was confirmed with fluoroscopy demonstrating the catheter tip was high in the
right atrium.  The Amplatz wire was reinserted and the catheter was advanced
further into the right atrium.  The wire was removed.  Both lumens withdrew
blood and flushed easily.  Catheter was secured with 0 silk sutures.  Venotomy
site was closed with a ___ Prolene subcuticular stitch.  Clean sterile
dressings were applied.  No immediate post-procedural complications.  The
patient tolerated the procedure well.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a tunneled hemodialysis/pharesis catheter
via a right internal jugular vein approach.  The tip is located in the right
atrium and the catheter is ready to use.
